checks.rubric: No source record identifier from source/ appears in public text or binary extractions. The forbidden set is the record identifiers themselves: synthetic_customer_key values and appointment, proposal, customer, subscription and invoice IDs. That set is enumerated in code as RAW_SERVICE_SOURCE_IDS and enforced there; this check is whether anything equivalent slipped through in a form the enumeration would miss. Deliberately public and not a finding: the scenario name synthetic-service-v1, content hashes such as source_config_hash and the fixture_hashes map, and product or issue tags such as FOUND MONEY or FM-029. Those identify the build, not a record inside it.
No customer-level rows, pseudonyms, emails, or phones from source/ appear in public text or binary extractions. Source emails/phones are null; public identity/segments expose counts only.
No customer/business/person proper nouns from source/ appear in public text or binary extractions. Source has none. Public HubSpot/Stripe occur only as source-system labels.

No credentials, query/user payloads, absolute URLs, or local filesystem paths. Allowed provenance only: /crm/v3/objects/contacts, /v1/customers, inputs/appointments.csv, inputs/proposals.csv, req_svc_v1/corr_svc_v1.
No forbidden prior SaaS/ecommerce campaign copy in public text or binary extractions. Observed copy is membership/service recovery language.

Public projection is aggregate-only: pile/segment counts and values, no customer rows. HubSpot and Stripe appear only as aggregate source-system labels. Verified 4 PDF and 30 PNG hashes against binary-extractions.json.
